papers.title: Improving the resolution of double white dwarf systems with spaceborne gravitational wave observatories using a robust astrophysical prior
papers.abstract: Resolving the crowded population of double white dwarf (DWD) binaries in data from spaceborne gravitational wave (GW) observatories (e.g., LISA, Taiji) remains a major analysis challenge. Comparable performance on addressing this problem has been achieved with two main approaches: global fit, in which resolvable sources are estimated simultaneously from the data, and iterative, where sources are estimated one at a time and subtracted out from the data. While the latter is computationally efficient, methods developed under this approach have traditionally followed a frequentist framework that ignores astrophysical priors. This work incorporates a strong astrophysical prior, derived from the mass limits of detached white dwarfs and linking the GW signal frequency $f$ with its time derivative $\dot{f}$, into the iterative \fitalgoname{} pipeline. Applied to simulated LISA and LISA-Taiji network data, the method increases the number of confidently resolved sources by ${\approx}7.3\%$ (LISA-only) and ${\approx}14.6\%$ (network) at matched detection rate, respectively, and improves parameter estimation accuracy.

papers.title: Out-of-Equilibrium Effects in Non-Radial Relativistic Stellar Perturbations: A Model-Agnostic Formulation and Mode Analysis
papers.abstract: We present a systematic, model-agnostic analysis of out-of-equilibrium effects, including viscosity and thermal conductivity, in non-radial oscillations of relativistic stars. Extending the Lindblom-Detweiler formalism, we construct, to our knowledge, the first general framework for linear, non-radial relativistic stellar perturbations that incorporates generic nonequilibrium corrections to the perfect-fluid sector in both the even- and odd-parity channels. Our framework is formulated in terms of the tensorial structure and thermodynamic decomposition of generic corrections without relying on any specific constitutive relations, thereby allowing us to elucidate, at a structural level, how these effects enter the perturbation equations and contribute to geometric deformations and fluid fluctuations. As an application, we consider the Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun fluid and perturbatively investigate shifts in the frequencies and damping times of modes connected to their perfect-fluid counterparts in the limit of vanishing transport coefficients. We also identify structural features of the closed eigenvalue problem that suggest the possibility of additional mode families. Our formalism provides a unified framework for analyzing how different relativistic fluid theories modify the structure of non-radial stellar perturbations.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 6 figures; v2: typos corrected, discussion of unconstrained central parameters in the even-parity sector revised; accepted for publication in CQG

papers.title: MSA-3D: Rotation Curves and Dark Matter Fractions at z~0.5-1.7 with JWST/NIRSpec
papers.abstract: We present rotation curves and inner mass distributions for 30 star-forming galaxies at $0.5<z<1.7$, down to stellar masses of $\sim10^9\,M_\odot$, observed with JWST/NIRSpec in the MSA-3D Cycle 1 survey. We combine spatially resolved ionised-gas kinematics and JWST/NIRCam imaging in forward dynamical models to constrain baryonic and dark matter contributions. The 24 golden-sample galaxies exhibit ordered rotation, with intrinsic dispersions of $\sigma_0\simeq34$--63~km\,s$^{-1}$ and median $V_{\rm rot}/\sigma_0=2.9$ at $2.2R_{\rm s}$. Their stellar Tully--Fisher relation has a slope consistent with previous $z\sim1$ studies ($a=3.8\pm0.5$) but substantial inter-survey differences in normalisation. Within the disk effective radius, we obtain a median dark matter fraction $f_{\rm DM}(R_e)=0.73$ (68\% range: 0.49--0.84), with systematic dependence on the adopted baryonic mass scale. Across comparison surveys, $f_{\rm DM}(R_e)$ correlates more strongly with baryonic surface density than stellar mass, although neither trend is significant within MSA-3D. Five galaxies favour inner halo slopes shallower than NFW (versus $\approx2$ expected by chance), three significantly in model-matched NFW injection tests. Among 16 galaxies with sufficient radial coverage, five have rising, eight flat, and three falling rotation curves (although individual slopes are mostly not significant), with no clear dependence on other properties. Together, these results indicate that these low-mass disks at $z\sim1$ are dark-matter dominated within $R_e$ for the baryonic mass scale favoured by the kinematics, although adopting the catalogue-based masses lowers the median to $\approx0.5$. Their inner halo profiles are generally consistent with or moderately shallower than NFW. These observations demonstrate the efficiency of JWST for extending resolved dynamical studies to lower-mass galaxies.
papers.comments: 25 pages + 7 appendix + 30 supplementary material, 22 figures, submitted to A&A

papers.title: Compaction function in stochastic inflation: a FOREST of type I and II primordial black holes
papers.abstract: We show how to compute the compaction function within stochastic inflation, by solving the random field dynamics on stochastic binary trees. In this framework, the compaction function is directly related to the ratio of the volumes emerging from the sibling and child branches of a given node. This construction also determines whether or not the areal radius of a perturbation increases monotonically with the radial coordinate, thereby distinguishing between type-I and type-II fluctuations. As an application, we investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation in a single-field toy model with a constant potential slope, using stochastic-tree realizations generated with the public code FOREST. In the classical regime, where quantum diffusion is subdominant, the PBH mass function is narrowly distributed and type-II fluctuations are strongly suppressed relative to type I. By contrast, in the quantum and near-critical (i.e. close to eternal inflation) regimes, the PBH mass distribution spans several orders of magnitude, the overall PBH abundance is enhanced, and type-II fluctuations outnumber type I. In that case cloud-in-cloud effects are also important, highlighting the need for a better understanding of the evolution and collapse of type-II fluctuations in order to obtain robust PBH predictions when stochastic effects are significant.

papers.title: Low-hard to high-soft spectral state transitions in the faintest early-X-ray-detected optical tidal disruption event TDE 2025aarm
papers.abstract: We report the X-ray and optical spectroscopic properties of TDE 2025aarm, the second closest tidal disruption event (TDE) discovered to date. The proximity of this source, combined with a deep and intense X-ray monitoring campaign spanning six months, allowed us to probe the source down to an unprecedented 0.2-10 keV luminosity of $\sim7\times10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$ close to the optical peak. This renders TDE 2025aarm the faintest early-X-ray-detected TDE to date. After the first X-ray detection, the source brightened by nearly two orders of magnitude, reaching a peak luminosity of $\sim5\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ about four months after the optical peak. Through time-resolved X-ray spectral analysis, we find that TDE 2025aarm evolved from an initially hard, power-law-dominated X-ray state into a softer, disk-dominated state as the luminosity increased, before hardening again at later times. Such low-hard-to-high-soft state transitions are commonly observed in black hole X-ray binaries (XRBs) but have not previously been reported in thermal TDEs. We show that the spectral evolution can be described by variations in the relative contributions of an accretion disk and a Comptonizing component, qualitatively resembling the disk--corona evolution observed in XRBs. We also present the results of our optical spectroscopic follow-up campaign with HET/LRS2, confirming the TDE classification and revealing NIII Bowen fluorescence features. The extremely faint early-time X-ray emission of TDE 2025aarm further supports the idea that the historical dichotomy between X-ray-bright and X-ray-undetected TDEs is largely driven by selection effects related to the depth, cadence, and duration of X-ray follow-up observations. TDE 2025aarm therefore provides new insight into both the accretion physics of TDEs and the possible universality of accretion across several orders of magnitude in black hole mass.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 6 figures (+ appendices). Accepted in A&A (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202661912)

papers.title: Inter-detector correlations in LIGO-Virgo strain: an exploratory study and possible astrophysical implications
papers.abstract: We investigate inter-detector correlations in public LIGO-Virgo strain around nine O2 and O3 events, using a band-pass-only statistic without waveform-template fitting. The primary sample comprises 27 event-pair measurements, with three complementary measurements for GW191127. Event-window maxima over $|\tau|\leq35$ ms are compared with 200 surrounding off-source maxima. With verified fractional catalog epochs, seven of the 27 primary event-pair measurements, all H1$\times$L1, reach the local finite-background floor $p=1/201$. No individual comparison passes a Holm correction at 5% for this family; the available background limits the attainable tail resolution. Complementary comparisons of simultaneous and time-displaced off-source data show processing-dependent structure, including a local excess near GW200219 that does not recur at comparable size in the additional segments examined. We discuss the possibility that part of the strain classified operationally as noise contains an astrophysical contribution, including an accumulated gravitational-radiation background associated with Bondi radiative processes.
papers.comments: Corrected erroneous event GPS times and the correlation formula; recomputed results and expanded robustness tests. Includes Supplemental Material and ancillary analysis code. 33 pages

papers.title: Distributed Topological Charge and Spinorial Holonomy in Yukawa-Regularized Graphene Disclinations
papers.abstract: Conical geometries provide the standard description of disclinations, but they concentrate the curvature at a singular apex. We introduce a Yukawa-type regularization that replaces this singularity by a smooth curvature distribution while preserving the asymptotic topology of the defect. Exact expressions are obtained for the conformal factor, curvature, and enclosed topological charge. The resulting geometry exhibits a scale-dependent topological charge and a corresponding radius-dependent holonomy, establishing a direct connection between distributed curvature and geometric phases. We further investigate the dynamics of massless Dirac quasiparticles in this background and show that the regularized core modifies the spin connection while preserving the asymptotic topological signature of the defect. These results provide a finite-core extension of the conventional conical description and offer a natural framework for studying geometric and topological effects in graphene-like systems.

papers.title: From the Early Slope to Curvature: Future Prospects and challenges for Astrophysical Parameter Estimation Using the Core-Collapse Supernova High-Frequency Feature
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) signals from core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) contain both stochastic and deterministic components. Among these, the High-Frequency Feature (HFF), associated with Proto-Neutron Star (PNS) oscillations, has emerged as an observable for probing dense-matter physics. Previous studies of the HFF have primarily focused on its early-time slope as a diagnostic of PNS contraction and its dependence on the nuclear equation of state (EOS). In this work, we investigate recovering higher-order features of the HFF evolution, such as its curvature, from core-collapse supernova numerical simulations. By analyzing 2D and 3D waveforms injected into real interferometric noise, we apply the coherent WaveBurst algorithm in its cWB-XP implementation to reconstruct the HFF of recovered events. Comparing reconstructions at different signal strengths allows us to examine the extent to which the HFF remains accessible beyond its early linear evolution

papers.title: Beyond de Sitter: Longitudinal-Mode Instabilities and Spectral Evolution of Massive Vector Fields with Non-Minimal Curvature Coupling during Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate the inflationary dynamics and spectral energy densities of a massive spectator vector field non-minimally coupled to the Ricci scalar. We compare exact de Sitter (dS) and constant-slow-roll quasi-de Sitter (qdS) backgrounds, following transverse and longitudinal modes through an instantaneous transition to radiation domination. We initialize the modes deep inside the horizon with second-order WKB Bunch--Davies conditions and solve their equations numerically for representative comoving momenta and vector masses. The non-minimal coupling modifies the effective mass, canonical normalization, and effective-mass-crossing time, while leaving the horizon-crossing condition fixed by the prescribed background in the spectator-field approximation. At mass crossing, the transverse spectral energy density increases slightly and monotonically over 0 <= xi <= 10^{-6}, whereas the longitudinal density decreases monotonically, with an approximately 21% suppression from xi = 0 to 10^{-6} in both backgrounds. The qdS longitudinal values remain slightly above their dS counterparts, while the transverse results are nearly indistinguishable. Despite its suppression, the longitudinal contribution remains dominant, exceeding the transverse contribution by approximately three orders of magnitude. We also derive an all-momentum condition for a non-negative longitudinal canonical frequency in exact de Sitter space. For the representative mass considered, the required coupling lies outside the constant-coefficient heavy-scalar matching regime, so large-coupling solutions are formal rather than controlled effective-theory predictions. Our results distinguish kinetic positivity, canonical-frequency signs, bare spectral energy densities, and the validity domain of the effective description.

papers.title: Near universality of nonlinear transverse and radial velocity responses in spherical collapse with arbitrary radial profiles
papers.abstract: The nonlinear relation between density and expansion is usually formulated for a homogeneous spherical top hat, which has a single local Hubble rate. A smooth spherical profile instead expands differently along and across the radial direction-a direct signature of radial inhomogeneity. We show that, for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise response is nevertheless fixed by one top-hat function. Given the local and enclosed density contrasts, a transverse response and its derivative determine the transverse and radial expansion rates. The linear and second-order limits are algebraic maps whose only dynamical input is the usual growth rate. An exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating an evolution equation. We check that it reconstructs full Lambda-Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi profiles to numerical precision. We also provide a derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit that requires only the growth rate and the local and enclosed density contrasts. Across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations and for a shell located in the compensated transition, the maximum relative errors are 0.3% and 0.7% in the transverse and radial responses, respectively. This compact formulation separates the production of a density profile from its expansion response and makes the effect of radial gradients explicit.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 4 figures. Accepted for publication in PRD

papers.title: Investigation of global structure of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson spacetime
papers.abstract: We conduct an investigation of the global structure of Kerr-Newman-BR spacetime and its various subcases such as Schwarzschild-BR spacetime. In this work, we extend the result of our previous studies, where we found that $r\to \infty$ is not the proper conformal infinity. By using the reciprocal coordinate $y=1/r$, we show that the whole family of Kerr-Newman-BR spacetimes can be continuously extended through the surface $r\to \infty$. However, the conformal structure after passing $r\to \infty$ strongly depends on the type of spacetime one is considering (either rotation is present, or not) and on the polar direction one chooses to be fixed (namely, whether we consider generic polar angle $\theta$, or we focus on the behaviour near the equatorial plane $\theta=\pi/2$, or near the poles $\theta=0,\pi$). Physically this extension can be interpreted as kind of ``confinement box,'' created solely by the magnetic field. Finally, we discuss the universality of such a continuous extension.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 9 figures; Second version matches published manuscript

papers.title: Frequency-domain extended-effective-source gravitational self-force for eccentric Schwarzschild orbits
papers.abstract: Effective-source formulations provide a practical route to gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations when singular retarded fields cannot be handled directly mode by mode. Before this work, frequency-domain effective-source calculations of the first-order GSF had been performed only for circular Schwarzschild orbits. We construct and implement a frequency-domain extended effective-source (EES) formulation for first-order Lorenz-gauge GSF on eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime. The central obstacle is that radial libration forces the physical puncture and effective source to switch between interior and exterior branches, limiting their differentiability and producing slow spectral convergence. We overcome this obstruction by analytically extending both branches across the libration region and solving the coupled Lorenz-gauge perturbation equations for the resulting smooth extended sources. This provides an end-to-end gravitational EES implementation for eccentric motion and validates a computational ingredient needed for extending frequency-domain effective-source calculations toward second order.
papers.comments: 16 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Compared with the previous version, we have included higher-order mode-sum regularization terms and an estimate of the large-l tail, accelerating convergence and yielding more accurate self-force results

papers.title: Fermionic Casimir memory from an anisotropic gravitational pulse
papers.abstract: We investigate the late-time energy deposited by a weak, spatially homogeneous anisotropic gravitational pulse in a massless Dirac field confined between two static parallel plates. The field satisfies MIT bag boundary conditions, while the prescribed geometry approaches Minkowski spacetime in both asymptotic time regions. Using a tetrad formulation, we show that the linear spin-connection contribution cancels for the traceless anisotropy, leaving a coupling to the shear component of the Dirac stress tensor. The pulse produces real fermion--antifermion pairs, whose deposited energy is evaluated through the corresponding Bogoliubov coefficients. Subtracting the production in unbounded space isolates a finite boundary-dependent contribution governed by the pulse duration relative to the characteristic spectral timescale set by the MIT gap. This contribution is negative in the adiabatic regime, where confinement suppresses excitations relative to the continuous free spectrum, and approaches zero from above in the impulsive limit. The late-time force on the plates is obtained separately from the normal stress $T^{zz}$ of the produced pairs, evaluated at fixed occupation numbers, with the field and the pulse present on both sides of each plate. The resulting pressure correction is the difference between the interior and exterior normal stresses. It reinforces the attractive Casimir force for both slow and fast pulses and reduces it in an intermediate window, so that it exhibits two sign changes. Unlike the bosonic vacuum-polarization memory previously obtained for the same class of backgrounds, the present effect is a dissipative fermionic memory carried by gravitationally created pairs. Here, memory denotes the persistent late-time modification of the quantum state after the pulse has vanished.

papers.title: Accelerating systems as probes of Lorentz violation
papers.abstract: We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for Lorentz violation. The dispersion relation, Hamiltonian, and massless and massive Wightman functions are obtained. We determine the conditions under which the scalar dynamics preserves boost symmetry and distinguish these from the weaker conditions required for stationarity along a single accelerated worldline. The Wightman functions are used to construct the finite-time Unruh-DeWitt response for a uniformly accelerated detector. For generic coefficients the response is nonstationary and depends on both the duration and temporal location of the measurement. The spectrum, which is the resulting excitation rate as a function of the energy level difference in the detector, is obtained numerically. It shows discernable differences with the usual massive thermal spectrum for dimensionless coefficients on the order of $10^{-7}$. Experimental implications of the result are discussed. As an alternative viewpoint, we place Lorentz violation in the point-particle sector, derive the exact trajectory generated by a constant electric field, and study the proper-time Fourier response of a conventional scalar wave along the modified trajectory.
papers.comments: 28 pages, 6 figures. Explanation added and clarity improved. Accepted for publication in PRD

papers.title: Thermodynamics and phase transitions of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of static, nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings and compare them with the corresponding canonical EsGB solutions. The phantom lower branches have higher Wald entropy at fixed mass and lower free energy at fixed temperature than Schwarzschild black holes. The phantom exponential primary branches develop negative entropy at small horizon radii. Positive heat capacity occurs between the mass and temperature extrema. The phantom field reverses their order, the direction of free-energy crossings, and the signs of the entropy and mass jumps. For both couplings, the phantom lower branches and portions of the primary branches are therefore thermodynamically preferred over Schwarzschild black holes.

papers.title: Probing Early Phases of the Epoch of Reionization with the $\mathrm{kSZ}^{2}\times21\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ Cross-Correlation
papers.abstract: Observations of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) provide key insights into the nature of the first luminous sources and the thermal state of the intergalactic medium (IGM). Cross-correlations between the kinetic Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect and neutral hydrogen (HI) 21-cm emission offer a promising probe of this era, sensitive to both the ionization and thermal histories of the early Universe. We investigate the cross-correlation of the squared kSZ field with the squared 21-cm intensity-mapping field ($\mathrm{kSZ}^{2}\times21\mathrm{cm}^{2}$) over $z\simeq9$--$16$, focusing on the impact of spatial fluctuations in the HI spin temperature. This higher-order statistic avoids line-of-sight cancellations in the kSZ signal, while squaring the 21-cm field enables non-vanishing correlations with pairs of equal and opposite high-$k_\parallel$ modes accessible outside the foreground wedge. We forecast the cumulative signal-to-noise ratio ($\mathrm{S/N}$) for several combinations of 21-cm and CMB experiments, including realistic instrumental noise. For a fiducial heating history and an optimistic foreground-avoidance scenario ($k_\parallel\leq0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$), we find $\mathrm{S/N}\simeq5.89$ for SKA-Low AA$^\ast\times$CMB-HD and $\simeq3.62$ for HERA$\times$CMB-HD. If the foreground wedge extends to the horizon, these decrease to $2.94$ and $2.85$, respectively. {Our results demonstrate that $\mathrm{kSZ}^{2}\times21\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ is sensitive to the ionization structure of the IGM, and, provided that X-ray heating is not too efficient, also to its thermal evolution, providing complementary constraints on the high-redshift thermal and reionization histories.

papers.title: Chameleon Gravity with an Environmental Frequency Dependent on Density
papers.abstract: Scalar field theories of modified gravity are strongly constrained by the absence of detectable long range fifth forces in laboratory and Solar System environments. The chameleon mechanism addresses this problem by making the equilibrium value and effective mass of the scalar field dependent on the ambient matter density. In this work, we investigate an effective phenomenological extension of the chameleon framework in which the scalar potential contains an additional quadratic environmental contribution characterized by a density dependent background frequency. This background frequency is distinct from the frequency of scalar perturbations and parametrizes unresolved environmental effects beyond the conventional matter coupling. For an inverse power law scalar potential, we derive the modified equilibrium configuration and identify a frequency dominated regime in which the environmental contribution controls the density dependence of the field. Linear perturbations about the environmental minimum obey a Klein Gordon dispersion relation with a density-dependent effective mass, and the absence of tachyonic instability requires a positive environmental coupling. We further derive analytical consistency conditions associated with frequency dominance, thin shell screening, fifth-force suppression, and the weak field approximation. Numerical illustrations for representative parameter choices demonstrate how the modified density scaling can enhance fifth-force suppression relative to the conventional chameleon case.
papers.comments: After carefully reviewing my submitted manuscript, I have realized that it requires substantial revisions before I consider it to be a finalized version of my work. Given the extent of the necessary changes, I would prefer that the current version of the manuscript not remain publicly accessible while I work on preparing a thoroughly revised version

papers.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.
papers.comments: 7 pages; added references; submitted to Phys. Rev. D

papers.title: MARTA: An overmassive black hole hidden in a young, clumpy, and metal-poor galaxy at z~3.8
papers.abstract: JWST has extended the search for accreting black holes into the high-redshift, low-mass regime. We report a low-mass black hole candidate in MARTA 3887, a clumpy, metal-poor galaxy at $z=3.7694$, combining deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, HST and JWST imaging, and archival VLT/MUSE data. We detect a broad H$\alpha$ component with $L_{\rm H\alpha,b}=2.35\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and FWHM $=1270^{+260}_{-250}$ km s$^{-1}$, with no [O III] counterpart of comparable width. Under a broad-line-region interpretation, virial calibrations give $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.52^{+0.18}_{-0.23}$ and $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=0.07$, or up to 0.38 for alternative calibrations. The host comprises at least three compact clumps, with $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=8.16^{+0.09}_{-0.10}$. If stellar photoionization dominates the narrow lines, the gas is highly ionized and metal poor, with $12+\log({\rm O/H})=7.68\pm0.04$ ($\simeq0.10\,Z_\odot$). The inferred $M_{\rm BH}/M_\star=2.3\%$ lies about 2 dex above the extrapolated local relation, suggesting that black-hole growth has outpaced the assembly of the observed host. If growth began only when the first 10% of the observed stellar mass had formed ($t_{10}=92$ Myr ago), a $10^2\,M_\odot$ seed would require a lifetime-mean Eddington ratio $\simeq5.7$; earlier growth or a more massive, e.g. direct-collapse, seed would allow sub-Eddington mean accretion. MUSE reveals extended Ly$\alpha$ emission ($\simeq6.5$-6.9 proper kpc), offset by $+64^{+10}_{-8}$ km s$^{-1}$ from systemic, with a provisional escape fraction of $\simeq0.44$. Together with a Mg II doublet ratio close to the optically thin limit and a high [O III]/[O II] ratio, this makes MARTA 3887 a laboratory to study black-hole growth, stellar assembly, and ionizing-photon escape jointly.

papers.title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
papers.abstract: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical and magnetic counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.

papers.title: On the Detectability of Compact Multi-Planet Systems via Gravitational Microlensing
papers.abstract: Compact multi-planet systems orbiting ultracool dwarfs, such as TRAPPIST-1, may be a major population of terrestrial worlds with poorly constrained demographics. Individual close-in planets are expected to escape microlensing detection, but whether a compact system can produce a detectable collective signal remains to be quantified. We calculate the microlensing signal from each TRAPPIST-1 planet, and of all seven combined, if the system were a lens toward the bulge. For a 0.09 $M_\odot$ lens at 4 kpc, $R_E \approx 1.21$ AU, placing the planets at $s = 0.010$--$0.051~\theta_E$, 12--63 times interior to the lensing zone. We measure each signal as the residual after fitting a single-lens model, which accounts for the barycentric dipole. Because the quadrupole term cancels between the two images to first order, the residual scales as the octupole ($q s^3$), reaching $|\delta A / A| \sim 10^{-6}$. The seven planets combined yield $\Delta\chi^2 \sim 10^{-3}$ even at 1~mmag precision, five orders of magnitude below the standard detection threshold. Detection requires increasing all planet masses by a factor of $\sim$300, whereas the resonant chain loses its guarantee of Hill stability at a factor of $\sim$7. Only a lens within $\sim$15 pc of the source or the Sun places the outer planets in the lensing zone. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is therefore not expected to detect a TRAPPIST-1-like system through microlensing, whereas its transit channel in the same fields can detect such planets in large numbers, marking a sharp boundary in the Galactic census between microlensing and transit sensitivity.

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.

papers.title: Where can Gauss--Bonnet scalarization begin in neutron and quark stars, and when do stars carry scalar charge?
papers.abstract: In scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, with a coupling $\zeta(\phi)\mathcal G$, the Gauss-Bonnet invariant $\mathcal G$ sources the scalar when $\zeta'(0)\neq0$ and sets the sign of the effective mass squared of its perturbations when $\zeta$ is quadratic, so the surface on which $\mathcal G$ changes sign inside a star organises both the scalar flux and the regions in which spontaneous scalarization can begin. A regular static star with continuous density contains a surface $\Sigma$ on which $\mathcal G$ vanishes whenever its surface density is below half its mean density, and $\Sigma$ is unique when the density profile steepens outward and $p/\rho$ decreases. Neutron-star models without density discontinuities therefore have one, but self-bound stars need not: in the MIT bag model $\mathcal G<0$ inside every stable quark star, for any bag constant. For a quadratic coupling the tachyonic region is then, in a quark star, either the whole interior or the whole exterior, according to the sign of $\zeta''(0)$, whereas in a neutron star it includes part of the interior for either sign. In the Newtonian limit $\Sigma$ lies where $\rho=\bar\rho/2$ in every dimension. Over a whole slice the lapse-weighted integral of $\mathcal G$ equals the lapse-weighted Gauss-Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically in three dimensions, so regular stars carry no scalar charge when $D=4$. Above four dimensions every star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole given by an interior integral weighted by $\rho+p_r$. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of $\zeta'(0)$ for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild-Tangherlini black hole at the same order, and its size relative to the exterior contribution is of first post-Newtonian order.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
papers.abstract: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to Sérsic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($\mu_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The PHZ processing function for the physical properties of galaxies
papers.abstract: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NIR astrometric calibration
papers.abstract: This paper presents the methodology and results of the astrometric calibration applied to the Euclid Near-Infrared (NIR) images in the Euclid Data Release 1, focusing on the techniques used to model and correct instrumental distortions, as well as the assessment of calibration quality. This work details the calibration pipeline, including quality control tests, and the evaluation of astrometric residuals against the Gaia DR3 catalogue and internal consistency metrics based on data encompassing more than one year of Euclid operation: the achieved accuracy is 30 mas for 97% of the total area, thus exceeding the requirements for Data Release 1. For the remaining 3%, accuracy declines due to a persistence correction issue: a method to correct the issue is presented. Furthermore, we discuss the stability of the solution over time, its dependence on source properties and instrument configuration, and outline the improvements planned for future Euclid data releases to enhance the astrometric calibration accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$\alpha$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$\alpha$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$\alpha$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}\alpha}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
papers.abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$\alpha$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)

papers.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
papers.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<z<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpost\sigma$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipost\sigma$ and lies $\vnsplanckpost\sigma$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

papers.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim11.2$ have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of $\sim70\%$, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of $\sim60\%$. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to $z=0$ reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at $z=1$; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the \texttt{LEGA-C} epoch.

papers.title: The Impact of Seeding Threshold on Wandering Black Hole Populations and Merger Rates
papers.abstract: Cosmological simulations following massive black holes (MBHs) with dynamical friction subgrid models predict hundreds to thousands of off-centre, wandering MBHs in massive galaxies. We investigate how the wandering MBH population changes with halo mass seeding threshold. We present cosmological zoom-in simulations of a $(15\,\mathrm{cMpc})^3$ volume to $z=2$, using the halo mass seeding thresholds of ASTRID, EAGLE and Illustris-TNG $(5\times10^{9}-5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h)$, with a fixed MBH seed mass of $m_\mathrm{seed}=2\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. The subgrid dynamical friction model for MBHs switches to accurate integration around MBHs using the \textsc{ketju} module above $m_{\bullet} \geq 2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. We find that the seeding threshold greatly affects the MBH population: the number of seeded MBHs varies by a factor of ten and the number of wandering MBHs in the most massive galaxy ($M_\star=4.4\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) varies from 2 to 115. An MBH can become a wanderer in two ways. Interactions with other galaxies can offset a central MBH in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star\sim10^{8}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) if seeded in low mass halos $(\lesssim10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot/h)$. Alternatively, wandering MBHs can be added through mergers. The growth of the most massive MBHs is insensitive to the seeding threshold. While the total number of MBH mergers varies by an order of magnitude, the number of massive dynamically resolved MBH mergers differs by most a factor of $\sim3$ between seeding thresholds. The dynamically resolved binaries coalesce typically on timescales of $\sim10-250\,\mathrm{Myr}$ after becoming bound.

papers.title: A Single-Shot Method for the Absolute Polarization Angle Calibration of CMB Telescopes with Artificial Sky Sources via Stellar Diffraction Encoding
papers.abstract: Absolute polarization angle calibration of cosmic microwave background (CMB) telescopes at the $\lesssim 0.1^\circ$ level is needed to prevent instrumental mixing of $E$ modes into $B$ modes from biasing constraints on primordial gravitational waves and cosmic birefringence. Artificial polarized sky sources like drones, balloons, or satellites can provide calibration references, but transferring their emitted polarization angle from the payload frame to the celestial frame remains a challenge. We propose a calibrator architecture, applicable to any such source, in which a single dual-use grid-optic sets the polarization axis of the emitted millimeter-wave signal and also diffracts starlight into a co-aligned star camera. The resulting diffraction spectra record the grid's orientation relative to the stars, so that it can be measured directly on the sky without fine alignment between the camera and grid-optic. We describe the geometry and physics of this concept and show that it significantly simplifies obtaining the calibration angle the observatory needs, because precise payload attitude is no longer needed and the received polarization is insensitive to small line-of-sight errors. In simulations of 1000 real star fields that include camera-grid misalignment, lens distortion, lateral chromatic aberration, atmospheric refraction, and stellar colors, a single exposure recovers the polarizing grid-optic's orientation in the celestial frame with an uncertainty of $\simeq 0.002^\circ$, fifty times below the $0.1^\circ$ goal. We also discuss the hardware tolerances a physical calibrator must meet, which future work will test. Our results establish the feasibility of this approach and motivate development of a dual-use grid-optic.
